problems.location: Bottom line, bullet 2, first sub-bullet: "SK hynix's optimised TSV-film process, with its IR inspection and FIB cross-section checks, was 'successfully applied in mass production' [C] PAPM-222."
problems.explanation: The JSTS full text applies the mass-production sentence to the optimised TEOS SiO2 deposition recipe: 'The optimized process was successfully applied in mass production ... with no significant differences in yield or inspection results.' The IR inspection image (Fig. 6) and the FIB cross-section comparison (Fig. 14) were used to qualify the recipe change. The paper does not say they are routine production inspection steps. The FIB cross-section is a one-off step-coverage comparison. Bundling the checks into the production claim turns a deposition-recipe claim into a production-inspection claim. The bullet heading ('Production wording for an HBM-line inspection or measurement step') depends on that.
problems.exact_fix:
- **Production wording near HBM-line inspection or measurement comes only from SK hynix, and only as its own untestable claims:**
  - SK hynix says its optimised TSV-liner (TEOS SiO2) deposition recipe was "successfully applied in mass production" with "no significant differences in yield or inspection results" [C] PAPM-222. The paper used its CVD-film IR inspection image and FIB cross-sections to qualify that recipe change and does not say they are routine production inspection steps [F] PAPM-219, PAPM-221.

problems.location: Bottom line, bullet 2, second sub-bullet: "SK hynix's in-line optical chip-warpage method for HBM is a 'commercialized solution currently in use' [C] PAPM-201."
problems.explanation: PAPM-201 says the results were 'implemented into measurement equipment and developed into a commercialized solution currently in use'. PAPM-202 says the method 'has been transferred to measurement equipment suppliers' and commercialised as an LSCW solution. Neither row says the solution is in use on SK hynix's own HBM line, which the bullet heading ('HBM-line') implies.
problems.exact_fix: - SK hynix says its in-line chip-warpage method for HBM was "implemented into measurement equipment and developed into a commercialized solution currently in use", after transfer "to measurement equipment suppliers"; the paper does not say where it is in use [C] PAPM-201, PAPM-202.

problems.location: Bottom line, bullet 4: "The non-electrical methods for bonded interfaces stay in development, with two exceptions:" followed by four sub-bullets
problems.evidence_ids: PAPL-046, PAPL-059, PAPM-212, PAPM-213, PAPM-216, SMP-016
problems.explanation: The heading announces two exceptions, but four sub-bullets follow. The first two (Intel NIR, Intel 100% overlay) are development items, not exceptions. The SK hynix item concerns micro-bump-stacked HBM, not hybrid bonds, and its 'by IR ... post-bond die shift and tilt' wording is supported by PAPM-212/213, which are not cited. 'Samsung ran in-line AFM' misattributes a Nearfield-led paper: per SMP-016, 13 of 23 authors are from Nearfield, including the first and last authors. SMP-016 also gives six wafers, not three.
problems.exact_fix:
- **Non-electrical methods for bonded interfaces stay in development:**
  - Intel's near-infrared post-bond overlay mapping is on a test vehicle [F] PAPL-046.
  - Intel's 100% chip-to-wafer overlay metrology is in development with a roadmap [F] PAPL-059.
- **Two items come closer to production, both short of a deployment statement:**
  - SK hynix validated IR measurement of post-bond die shift and tilt in micro-bump-stacked HBM (not hybrid bonds) "using actual HBM device wafers in a production-grade MI setup" [F] PAPM-212, PAPM-213, PAPM-216.
  - A Nearfield-led paper with ten Samsung co-authors reports in-line AFM "performed on production wafers in the fab" (six wafers) for V-NAND (not HBM) hybrid bonding [F] SMP-016.

problems.location: Bottom line, bullet 5: "X-ray appears as failure-analysis practice (ASE 3D X-ray microscopy [F] PAPL-107; Intel CT and synchrotron work [F] PAPL-067, PAPL-082)"
problems.explanation: PAPL-067 is 3D X-ray CT verifying TCB joint quality in process research for co-packaged optics, not failure analysis. PAPL-082 is speed-path debug by X-ray-assisted device alteration on a mock stacked die. There X-ray perturbs devices and does not inspect them. Neither is failure-analysis practice. The Intel X-ray CT paper that is FA (Intel/Comet de-warping of CT data, XR-023) is not cited.
problems.exact_fix: - X-ray appears in failure analysis (ASE 3D X-ray microscopy [F] PAPL-107; Intel CT de-warping with Comet, on FCPGA packages [F] XR-023), in process-research verification (Intel 3D X-ray CT of TCB micro-bump joints [F] PAPL-067), in post-silicon debug by X-ray-assisted device alteration on a mock stacked die (Intel, synchrotron [F] PAPL-082), as "examined" (Samsung [F] TALK-020), in a patent application (Samsung [F] XR-012) and as a stated concern about memory damage (Intel [F] XR-001; TSMC per press [S] XR-013).

problems.location: Bottom line, bullet 6: "Intel exposed on-package DRAM to 350 rad, which it calls three times the DRAM maker's limit, with no functional errors ... [F] XR-002, XR-003."
problems.explanation: Intel's text (p54) gives '350 rads ... no errors' and then 'overexposure to three times the limit provided by DRAM manufacturer'. Reading 350 rad as that "three times" (a limit of about 117 rad) is my inference [I] XR-035, Low.

problems.location: Section 0, item 3: "Neither memory maker says its HBM is hybrid-bonded today. ... Production statements about hybrid bonding exist only for wafer-to-wafer V-NAND (Samsung, Section 1) and outside memory."
problems.explanation: The scope has three memory makers, so 'Neither' is wrong; Micron's position (TALK-021, an 'outlook' talk) is not mentioned. The first and last sentences carry no tag. Calling the Samsung/Nearfield V-NAND item a 'production statement' contradicts Section 5, which rates it PILOT ('validated on production wafers ... without a deployment statement'), and the bottom line, which treats it as an exception short of production. 'and outside memory' has no evidence: no in-period document read gives a production statement for hybrid-bonding inspection outside memory, and item 4 says no TSMC SoIC method was found. TALK-034 comes from an undated product page, which should be said.
problems.exact_fix: 3. **"Hybrid-bonded HBM" as a current product.** None of the three memory makers says in a document read that its HBM is hybrid-bonded today [I] TALK-014, TALK-021, TALK-034. A guest tech note by Prof. Seunghwan Joo (Inha University), hosted on SK hynix's newsroom in August 2026, says die-to-wafer hybrid bonding for HBM is "progressing toward commercialization". That is not SK hynix's own statement [S] TALK-014. Samsung's undated HBM3E product-page FAQ says it is "preparing to adopt" hybrid copper bonding [C] TALK-034. Micron's VLSI 2025 workshop talk is an "outlook" for chip-to-wafer hybrid-bonded memory stacking [F] TALK-021. Inspection statements about hybrid-bonded HBM are therefore development statements. No in-period document read gives a production statement for a hybrid-bonding inspection or measurement step. The closest is in-line AFM "performed on production wafers in the fab" for V-NAND wafer-to-wafer hybrid bonding, in a Nearfield-led paper with Samsung co-authors, which Section 5 rates pilot [F] SMP-016.

problems.location: Section 0, item 7, second bullet: "SPIE records carry no affiliations. A SPIE paper is attributed to a company only where its abstract names the company; otherwise the attribution is [I]." (also Section 1 'How to read it': "a row tagged [I] is attributed to the chipmaker by inference (SPIE records without affiliations)")
problems.evidence_ids: SMP-016, SMP-017, PAPM-166, PAPM-171, PAPM-170, PAPM-165
problems.explanation: SPIE journal (J. Micro/Nanopatterning) Crossref records do carry affiliations: SMP-016 lists 10 Samsung and 13 Nearfield authors, and SMP-017 lists Samsung authors. The rule 'abstract names the company' also conflicts with the research question, which admits vendor material only where the company co-authors it. PAPM-171 ('evaluates the performance of this MBI tool on Micron Technology's DRAM') and PAPM-166 ('implemented in collaboration with Micron') name Micron's devices or collaboration, not Micron authorship, yet Section 1 tags them [F] as Micron documents.
problems.exact_fix: - SPIE proceedings records in Crossref carry no affiliations (SPIE journal records such as J. Micro/Nanopatterning do). A SPIE proceedings paper is attributed to a company only where its abstract or the company's own release names it as an author. Where the abstract names only the company's devices or says "in collaboration with" it (e.g. PAPM-166, PAPM-171), authorship is unknown and the paper may be vendor material, so the attribution is [I] (retag the Section 1 rows for 10.1117/12.3056182, 10.1117/12.3093590 and 10.1117/12.3092424 from [F] to [I]).
